status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: Instinct processed previously indexed personal email after the Google connector was disconnected. Live Gmail access had ended. The retained evidence does not establish the consent terms for continued processing or whether disconnection prohibited use of retained copies. Those terms determine the privacy and user-autonomy outcome.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence demonstrates a disconnect between revoking a live connector and terminating an AI agent's ability to process data already ingested from that connector. That distinction creates a user-control and data-lifecycle governance risk when disconnect semantics may reasonably be understood as ending the agent's effective use of connected-account data. The available evidence does not establish whether disconnecting Google created an operative control state that prohibited later processing of retained copies; separately, ending the live Gmail connector supports the bounded Authentication-State Continuity invariant-held mapping. The affirmative source distinction between terminated live access and retained-copy processing supports the bounded authentication success. The effective retained-data control scope remains unresolved; revocation does not automatically mean deletion or prohibition of previously ingested data use. Neither an access-continuity breach nor a consent/training duty is inferred without source-defined semantics.
